decision: FRAGILE-HYPOTHESIS-FALSIFIED-BUT-ECONOMICS-UNMEASURED — The frozen fragile hypothesis is FALSIFIED: break-even systematic bias is 33.3 tokens/task (far exceeds frozen F1 threshold of 3 tokens/task) and bootstrap survival is 96.1% under ±50% completion variation (far exceeds frozen F2 threshold of 70%). The margin is analytically robust to completion token estimation error under the frozen assumptions. However: (1) the audit V1_V_BREAK_EVEN_TAUTOLOGY identifies that systematic uniform bias cannot erase the margin by construction (margin is a difference), so the break-even threshold is only meaningful for differential bias; (2) the audit V2_V_BOOTSTRAP_SCALE_MISMATCH identifies that the bootstrap tests the 112-token selection savings, not the full 1067-token workflow margin, due to independent sampling dropping the 955-token completion offset; (3) critically, audit V4_V4_PURELY_ANALYTICAL_NO_LLM_MEASUREMENT confirms this is the fourth consecutive PRODUCT experiment with zero real LLM calls — the 5.42% margin is based entirely on analytical estimates (completion tokens 2/15/20 assumed, not measured). The absolute savings (1067 tokens, 5.42%) remain thin and the COLD baseline is analytically 7.5x cheaper. No product promotion. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS.

product_action: This is the fourth consecutive PRODUCT lane experiment without real LLM measurement (two MEASUREMENT_INVALID no API keys, one SURVIVES tautological, one analytical sensitivity). The parent handoff's three-way decision (A/B/C) remains unresolved but the sensitivity analysis clarifies the landscape: (A) provision LLM API credentials and execute frozen COLD baseline — justified by robust margin, requires external human action to configure OPENAI_API_KEY; (B) close C-PRODUCT-ECON — the 5.42% margin is thin and based on estimates even if analytically robust, COLD is 7.5x cheaper, and 4 consecutive experiments without real measurement suggests infrastructure is the binding constraint; (C) pivot to measuring end-to-end agent economics on real SPIDER registry — requires new frozen design. The Director recommends option B (close C-PRODUCT-ECON) because: (1) four consecutive failures to produce real LLM measurement indicate a persistent infrastructure blocker, not a transient gap; (2) the absolute margin (5.42% of estimated tokens) is not economically meaningful at current scale; (3) COLD at 77 tokens/task is 7.5x cheaper analytically; (4) the product lane should redirect to non-token mechanisms (registry compression, retrieval efficiency, correctness improvements) that have higher information gain. No product promotion.

reason: The frozen fragile hypothesis is falsified: the 5.42% margin is analytically robust to completion estimation error (break-even 33.3 tokens/task, survival 96.1%). However, this does not resolve C-PRODUCT-ECON because: (1) the margin is thin and based on analytical estimates, not real LLM measurement; (2) four consecutive PRODUCT experiments have produced zero real LLM calls; (3) COLD is analytically 7.5x cheaper; (4) the audit ceiling is bounded to analytical sensitivity under frozen synthetic 32-task corpus with hard-coded 2/15/20 completion estimates. The claim cannot advance to EXPERIMENTAL without real end-to-end measurement. The product lane has exhausted the analytical token-cost line and should pivot to either (a) real LLM measurement if API access is provisioned, or (b) non-token product mechanisms with higher information gain.
